title: Canonical Forecast Point
description: Compact forecast row with numeric ranges and identity-only measurement-vendor references.

impression_basis.description: Experimental (media_buy.dooh_impression_basis). On a DOOH point that forecasts `impressions` from `plays`, the methodology tier the forecast uses, when it is the same for every expected play. When the point covers plays expected on different tiers, including the fallback plays a sensor-equipped screen is expected to estimate on `seller_modeled` while its sensor is not reporting, sellers MUST omit it, never substituting `hybrid` or the majority tier, and report `impression_basis_breakdown`; a point never carries both. Lets forecast and delivery reconcile on the same declaration. Sellers that emit it MUST list `media_buy.dooh_impression_basis` in `experimental_features`.

audience_multiplier.description: Experimental (media_buy.dooh_impression_basis). The planning multiplier of a single-tier DOOH point: `metrics.impressions.mid / metrics.plays.mid`, rounded. The impressions are authoritative: a receiver MUST NOT reject a multiplier that differs from that ratio only by rounding. A point that reports `impression_basis_breakdown` SHOULD omit it and give each entry's planning multiplier instead: a multiplier blended across tiers mixes different units and misleads. A declaration, not a forecastable metric, so it sits outside `metrics`.

impression_basis_breakdown.description: Experimental (media_buy.dooh_impression_basis). For a DOOH point covering plays expected on different tiers, one entry per tier with the expected plays and impressions behind the point's midpoints: at least two entries, whose tiers MUST be distinct and whose `plays` and `impressions` MUST sum exactly to `metrics.plays.mid` and `metrics.impressions.mid`, which a point carrying a breakdown therefore carries. It SHOULD include the fallback the seller expects: the plays sensor-equipped screens are expected to estimate on `seller_modeled` while their sensor is not reporting. A point never carries both this and `impression_basis`. Tiers are different units with no exchange rate, so compare impressions within a tier (and for `sensor_measured`, within the same metric), and plays and spend across tiers.
